messages:
oncall-bot: [ALERT] SLO burn-rate threshold crossed for /v1/generate (customer-facing). burn_rate=5.2 over 5m, SLO window=7d. auto-escalation: paging criteria met. Please acknowledge.

oncall-bot: Incident ID INC-2381 created: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2381. Runbook: /runbooks/slo-burn-response.md

Alex.k: acked. I'm on it. Checking recent deploys and routing.

Elaine: saw a small deploy 3m ago to routing-service, but can confirm no model change. grabbing logs for 5m window.

Sam.w: adding context — customer reports a few timeouts ~10s spikes on gen calls. Not widespread but enough to push burn.

Devops-jen: bringing up tail of requests: ```curl -s "https://metrics.api/query?m=slo.burn_rate&range=5m" | jq .``` Getting only a few hosts with elevated cpu. forwarding host list.

Alex.k: running quick mitigation: throttling low-priority background inference queue to reduce contention. Command: `kubectl patch hpa bg-infer -p '{"spec": {"minReplicas": 0}}'`

Elaine: confirmed background queue down. CPU dropped on two hosts, but burn still at ~4.6. Looks like a KV cache pressure — cache miss spikes correlated.

Sre-lead: if KV cache misses are root, we should avoid mass restarts. Plan: 1) keep bg queue throttled 2) enable prefix caching for hot-models 3) temporary alert threshold relax for only high-noise window and notify paging recipients. Thoughts?

Alex.k: agree with conservative approach. For (3) we can adjust the burn-rate alert to require sustained >4 for 10m instead of 5m to reduce noisy pages while we stabilize.

Product-ops: customer impact note: a handful of power-users saw degraded latency, escalations to support are at 3 tickets so far. Please add an incident annotation for customer comms.

Sam.w: doing a handoff — I'm tagged for the next 20m while Alex and Elaine keep looking at cache metrics. If we relax the alert window, make sure our dashboard shows a short-term spike bar so ops don't miss regressions.

Alex.k: creating a quick dashboard panel: "SLO burn (5m,10m,30m)" — link (temp): https://observability.redwood/d/quick/INC-2381

Devops-jen: patch to alert rule proposed: ```- alert: SLOBurnHigh
  expr: slo:burn_rate:ratio[10m] > 4
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "SLO burn > 4 over 10m for /v1/generate"```

Elaine: note — changing `for` to 10m will suppress immediate flapping pages but still page for sustained issues. ok from my side.

Oncall-bot: Proposed: do not alter paging recipients; only gate on `for` change. Also tagging runbook that threshold change must be reverted within 24h or after incident closes.

Sre-lead: approve temporary change. Sam, Alex — please deploy the alert patch with `--dry-run` then real. Track in INC-2381.

Sam.w: deploying alert patch now: `flux reconcile kustomization alerts --with-source` (will monitor).

Alex.k: while alert settles, I'm going to scale a healthy cache replica up to absorb hot prefixes: `kubectl scale deploy/kv-cache --replicas=5`

Devops-jen: scaled. Cache hitrate jumped from 72% -> 88% on affected shards. Great.

Elaine: seeing error gap narrow. Customer tickets show fewer new complaints in last 8m.

Product-ops: adding an incident note for customer comms: "We observed elevated latency for a subset of users; mitigation applied and services stabilized. Followup postmortem planned."

Sre-lead: OK team — since we moved threshold `for` to 10m, confirm in INC-2381 timeline and add a follow-up action for alert tuning: we need multi-window detection rather than single-window. Put as action item: "create composite alert: (burn_1m > x AND burn_10m > y) OR sustained 10m burn"

Alex.k: filing a ticket: ALERT-1298 "Composite multi-window SLO burn rule" with proposed thresholds and test harness.

Sam.w: handoff note: I'm stepping off rotation in 15m. Alex will be primary; Elaine will monitor cache. Leaving a quick checklist in thread: - alert `for` increased to 10m (temp) - bg queue throttled - cache replicas scaled - dashboard created - ticket ALERT-1298 created - annotate incident for customer comms

Alex.k: thanks @sam.w — I have it. I'll keep monitoring for next 40m, then put a revert plan scheduled if stable for 1h.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2381 update: mitigations applied, customer impact reduced, incident severity lowered to S2. Next update at +30m or on change.

Sre-lead: post-incident follow-up items assigned: - ALERT-1298 (Alex) - Runbook cache-ops update (Elaine) - Pager criteria doc update to include multi-window composite (Devops-jen)

Product-ops: will draft a short customer-facing blurb for support to send if more tickets come in.

Sam.w: leaving final note: small night follow-up: replicate the cache hit improvement to staging and run a load test to confirm no regression.

Elaine: copy. I'll run the staging test and post results here.

Alex.k: closing handoff. Good coordination everyone. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2381 resolved to monitoring state at 2381234700. Reminder: temporary alert change must be reverted or documented within 24h.
